angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 191,318 km at 30.50 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 32.7823 +/- 0.0140 mas (same row, RUWE 1.41): 30.50 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.275 +/- 0.009 solar radii from Cadieux et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1452 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...96C/abstract): 191,318 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.249 +/- 0.008 solar masses from Cadieux et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1452 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...96C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3185 +/- 50 K from Cadieux et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1452 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...96C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cadieux et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1452 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...96C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1452.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.956, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
